brief: The Market Ear argues the real bubble sits in consumer staples, not technology. S&P staples' valuation premium to the S&P 500 is at its highest level in over 10 years, while tech's forward P/E is near its COVID-crash low, the inverse of the consensus AI-bubble narrative (cited to Puro Saxena). Historically, after similar staples rallies, relative returns over the following three months have typically turned negative. Hedge funds have reinforced the move: short covering unwound gross exposure, leaving them net long staples for the first time since October 2025. Staples beat tech by 33% over the last 30 days, the largest such gap in about 25 years, with the only comparable stretch being April 2000 through October 2001. Staples have also outperformed consumer discretionary as investors pay up for safety, and staples credit spreads have compressed over recent years. The final irony: staples' forward dividend yield relative to the 10-year Treasury sits at the 1st percentile, so despite being defensive, staples are priced expensively, not cheaply.
